In its first post-election poll, the Economist/YouGov series has found the president 26 points underwater, with 36 percent approving of his job performance and 62 percent disapproving, a seven-point deterioration from the pollster’s final survey before Election Day.

That shift could be significant for Republican lawmakers deciding how closely to align themselves with a president whose core supporters remain loyal but whose broader standing could complicate the party’s recovery. President Donald Trump’s job approval rating sits at 32% in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll, with 65% disapproving, as the survey was conducted Nov. 6-9 among 1,705 U.S. adults.

An Economist/YouGov poll found just 32% approving while 63% disapproved of Trump’s job performance, including 52% who disapproved strongly.

Sixty-one percent of respondents disapproved of Trump’s foreign policy and 67% disapproved of his handling of the economy. [...] Thirty-nine percent of respondents said there should be some or a lot of focus on investigating the Trump administration, while 40% said there shouldn’t be.
